newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ex-Soviet Moldova seeks soft entry to WTO.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet Moldova seeks soft entry to WTO.

text.p: Former Soviet Moldova, pleading for understanding for its serious economic problems, on Tuesday asked to be allowed into the World Trade Organisation (WTO) as a developing country.

The request was presented to a meeting of trade envoys from the current 131-member WTO, with a Moldovan delegation headed by deputy economy and reform minister Dumitru Braghis to discuss the entry application.

"Despite all efforts made at the macro-economic level including a conversion programme and agricultural reform, we have not achieved macro-economic growth as most of our companies are in decline while others are struggling to survive," Braghis told a WTO working party.

The country, a former Romanian territory mainly incorporated into the Soviet Union after World War Two and independent since 1991, was also burdened by total dependence on external sources of energy, he said.
Because of these problems, Braghis told the WTO envoys, Moldova was requesting "a certain flexibility" and would be seeking entry to the body as a developing country.

If such terms are agreed, the landlocked state of 4.5 million people would only have to bring its economic policies into line with WTO open trading rules gradually, within timeframes to be agreed with current members.

Trade sources said the appeal was initially given a sympathetic hearing by key powers including the European Union, the United States and Japan -- although many urged Moldova to start implementing the reforms it would need to make.
The United States told Braghis it would like to see his country declare a standstill on current rules affecting trade in goods and services while the accession talks were under way.

Major powers have asked Russia, also bidding for WTO entry, for a similar commitment -- which would bar any measures hardening present practices which run against the trade body's rules -- but Moscow has refused. Russia is asking for admission as a developed power.
China, in negotiation for entry for over a decade and also seeking developing country status, has agreed to a standstill.
Moldova applied to join the WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), in 1993, but negotiations were stalled by its economic and political problems.
Of the 15 republics of the former Soviet Union, 14 have applied to join the WTO. Only Turkmenistan has yet to submit an application.
